title: TangoFlux: Super Fast and Faithful Text to Audio Generation with Flow Matching and Clap-Ranked Preference Optimization
claim: A two-stage training recipe, supervised pre-training followed by an online loop of sampling, ranking and preference optimization, produces the final model.
layout: 2 grey panels, left-to-right; vertical flow in pre-training, cyclic dashed feedback loop in alignment; legend box on top
description: Two rounded grey panels read left to right. Panel 1, "Pre-training", shows a waveform passing through a frozen Stable Audio VAE encoder into a purple block of 6x MMDiT and 18x DiT layers, then decoded back to a waveform. Dataset pills (WavCaps, AudioCaps) feed flow-matching loss triangles, leading down to a purple "TangoFlux-base π0" box. A dotted arrow carries π0 into panel 2, "Online Iterative Alignment". There, prompt/audio pairs from AudioCaps go into policy πt. πt samples candidate audios, which a yellow CLAP scorer ranks into winner (green) and loser (red) audios. These feed an L_CRPO triangle that trains the next policy πt+1. A dashed loop returns πt+1 to the start, and an arrow leads to the TangoFlux logo. A legend at the top defines the symbols for sampling, training and dataset.
caption: A depiction of the overall training pipeline of TANGOFLUX.
abstract: We introduce TangoFlux, an efficient Text-to-Audio (TTA) generative model with 515M parameters, capable of generating up to 30 seconds of 44.1kHz audio in just 3.7 seconds on a single A40 GPU. A key challenge in aligning TTA models lies in the difficulty of creating preference pairs, as TTA lacks structured mechanisms like verifiable rewards or gold-standard answers available for Large Language Models (LLMs). To address this, we propose CLAP-Ranked Preference Optimization (CRPO), a novel framework that iteratively generates and optimizes preference data to enhance TTA alignment. We demonstrate that the audio preference dataset generated using CRPO outperforms existing alternatives. With this framework, TangoFlux achieves state-of-the-art performance across both objective and subjective benchmarks. We open source all code and models to support further research in TTA generation.
